column1: # Tolerances of the cases of test.tsv that need more than the general
# 1e-12 relative: function, relative bound, absolute bound, why. A number
# passes when it is within either bound. Read by cli/test.sh and by the
# Go, npm and Python tests. Measured on arm64 (fused multiply-adds) and
# with MSVC against the values of the R package on x86-64.

column4: gap is the residual at the stopping point, about 1e-10: its last digits are rounding
drift and dvdt are sums that cancel to about 1e-11 and 1e-19
a coefficient that is zero up to rounding (about 1e-16)
the short axis of the ellipse of a cluster whose points lie on a line: zero up to rounding (about 1e-10)
p is a tail probability of z: an error of 1e-13 in z gives 1e-12 in p
alpha is the minimum found by golden-section search, which the rounding of the objective fixes only to about 1e-8; se and ks follow it
fitted by BFGS to a tolerance of 1e-7; the estimates agree, the standard errors (curvature at the fitted point) to about 1e-9
the spatial coefficient is the minimum found by Brent's method, which rounding of the likelihood fixes to about 1e-7; the other estimates follow it
fitted by BFGS to a tolerance of 1e-7 on a likelihood that is flat near its maximum: the estimates agree to about 1e-4
two excitation coefficients are estimated at about 1e-10, zero up to the tolerance of the search: their last digits are rounding
p is a tail probability of the test statistic: an error of 1e-14 in it gives 1e-12 in a p of 1e-50

the standard errors come from a numerical inverse of the Hessian at the fitted point: on GitHub's x86-64 and arm64 runners they differ from the values of the R package by 4e-12 relative (0.5699719719486 against 0.5699719719508), the estimates by less
fitted by Nelder-Mead to a relative tolerance of 1.5e-8 on the likelihood: rounding of the objective changes the last digits of the parameters
without a variogram the model is fitted by Nelder-Mead first, to a relative tolerance of 1.5e-8
the range is the minimum found by Brent's method to a tolerance of 1.2e-4 in its log; the other estimates follow it
fitted by Nelder-Mead to a relative tolerance of 1e-6 on the restricted likelihood
theta and the zero-inflated fit are iterated to a tolerance, and their last digits follow the rounding of the scores
Newton-Raphson to a step of 1e-10 with a numerical Hessian: the standard errors carry its rounding, about 1e-10 relative
Newton-Raphson to a step of 1e-10 with a numerical Hessian: the standard errors carry its rounding, about 1e-10 relative
the factor is the place of a minimum found by Brent's method, known only to about the square root of the machine precision
least squares fits whose sums the R package runs through the BLAS in another order
eigenvalues and the inverse by other routines than LAPACK
EM iterated to a tolerance of 1e-7
fits by the Nelder-Mead and BFGS minimisers, stopped at their tolerances
cells that are zero up to rounding (about 1e-19): their digits differ between machines
entries of the centred matrix that cancel to rounding, about 1e-16
coordinates and stress that are zero up to rounding, and eigenvalues from an iteration
fitted by a quasi-Newton search with a numerical gradient: the last digits follow the rounding of the likelihood
fitted by a quasi-Newton search with a numerical gradient, a conditional stage then the exact likelihood

the fit iterates until the relative change of the deviance is below 1e-10: where rounding differs the last step can differ, which moves the estimates by about 1e-10; the bootstrap errors are sd() and cov() of the draws, which R sums in long double
the fixed effects are taken out by alternating projections to 1e-12 of each column, and p is a tail probability of the statistic: an error of 1e-14 in it gives 1e-12 in a small p
the Poisson fits iterate as in ppmlfe, on the full sample and on each bootstrap draw
its fit is ivfe() or, for norm = "pois", ppmlfe()
p is a tail probability of the statistic and the case's design has variance inflation factors above 30: on arm64 a p of 4.8e-21 differs by 4e-12 relative, the estimates by 1e-15

coefficients of time dummies that are small differences of cross-products: on arm64 an estimate of 0.004 differs by 6e-15 absolute, 1.4e-12 relative; the tests are tail probabilities of statistics built from them
the regressors are projected off the cross-section averages unit by unit, and what is left cancels to rounding where a regressor follows the averages closely
p is a tail probability of the F statistic: an error of 1e-14 in it gives 1e-12 in a small p
the covariance sums over strata in the order the rows arrive, which differs after the moving average drops days: last digits (about 1e-12)
local linear fits on few points beside the cut-off: sums that differ in the last digits with fused multiply-adds (about 1e-12)
the density estimates are ratios of weighted sums: last digits with fused multiply-adds (about 1e-12)
the exponential GMM estimate is iterated to a stopping rule: compilers and platforms stop within about 1e-9 of one another (measured 3e-9 on arm64, 2e-9 in the Linux wheel, 5e-10 with MSVC)

the spline surface of the reference case is close to collinear (condition number about 1e6, its joint test refused for rank): standard errors agree to about 1e-8 across compilers, a surface value near zero (5e-4) to about 4e-6
a grid point of the density that is zero up to rounding (about 1e-16) where the fused multiply-add gives another last bit
the same grid as plotrdg
